page: Amazon Web Services c9gd.4xlarge is a compute-optimized server type built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the 64-bit ARMv9 architecture. The system provides 16 dedicated physical cores using AWS Neoverse-V3 processors operating at 3.3 GHz. With a 1:1 thread-to-core configuration, the architecture eliminates resource contention from simultaneous multithreading. It is equipped with 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 32 GB, establishing a compute-focused ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not include a GPU accelerator.

Local storage is bundled directly via a 950 GB NVMe SSD instance store, providing fast scratch space with lower latency than network-attached block volumes. Baseline network throughput is rated at 8 Gbps. Synthetic benchmarks highlight strong core capability, with top-tier rankings in both Geekbench single-core (2443.0) and multi-core (20665.0) metrics, alongside top-tier results in PassMark memory testing. Data manipulation throughput is notable, reaching 36.4 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression and top-tier single-threaded bzip3 decompression. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth registers at 187.87 GB/sec, placing it in the top 25% of measured instances.

The instance presents specific engineering tradeoffs. The 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio restricts suitability for large in-memory caches or massive dataset analytics requiring substantial RAM footprints. Furthermore, the local NVMe storage is ephemeral, meaning persistent data storage must be managed externally. However, the high single-thread clock efficiency, hardware cryptographic acceleration via AES instructions, and fast local NVMe make the c9gd.4xlarge cost-efficient for compute-heavy and I/O-intensive tasks. Primary fit workloads include static web serving, software compilation, batch compression pipelines, lightweight LLM token generation, and distributed CI/CD build environments requiring rapid local disk access.
description: Amazon Web Services c9gd.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor and custom ARMv9 architecture. It delivers 16 dedicated physical cores running AWS Neoverse-V3 processors at 3.3 GHz without simultaneous multithreading, paired with 32 GB of system memory at a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The server bundles 950 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage and maintains an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, operating without discrete GPU acceleration. In benchmark assessments, the hardware achieves top-tier results in single-core and multi-core Geekbench processing, along with top-decile performance in text processing and data compression. Large-block memory read bandwidth and database operations demonstrate upper-quartile throughput. Because its memory allocation is constrained to 2.0 GB per vCPU, it is less suited for massive in-memory databases, but the combination of high-clocked dedicated cores and local high-speed disk makes it highly efficient for static web serving, high-throughput batch compression, continuous integration builds, and distributed I/O-heavy computing pipelines.
